meta.topStoryHeadline: Obama Presidential Center Opens on Juneteenth with Major Black Artist Commissions
meta.topStorySummary: The Obama Presidential Center opens June 19 on Juneteenth in Chicago's Jackson Park. The 19.3-acre, $850 million campus is anchored by site-specific commissions from Theaster Gates, Njideka Akunyili Crosby (official Obama portraits), Rashid Johnson, Lorna Simpson, and Martin Puryear. The opening ceremony on June 18 featured The Roots and Stevie Wonder.
executiveSummary: The Obama Presidential Center opens June 19 on Juneteenth in Chicago — commissions from Theaster Gates, Njideka Akunyili Crosby, Rashid Johnson, and Lorna Simpson anchor a 19.3-acre campus, one of the largest public art commissions in decades.

The 79th Tony Awards produced a historic night for Black theatre: Ruben Santiago-Hudson won Best Featured Actor for Joe Turner's Come and Gone, Joshua Henry won Best Actor for Ragtime, and Qween Jean became the first openly transgender person to win a Tony Award for Cats: The Jellicle Ball.

The federal arts funding crisis is deepening — NEA anti-DEI restrictions under Executive Order 14398, combined with Challenge America cuts, are falling hardest on Black arts institutions, most of which operate without reserves or endowments.

events.title: La Cage aux Folles — Encores!
events.description: All-Black production directed by Robert O'Hara, starring Billy Porter and Wayne Brady, timed to NYC Pride. Tonya Pinkins and Peter Francis James also star; Dormeshia choreographs tap. Closes June 28.

events.title: Blooming in Dry Season
events.description: New York premiere of a Caribbean family drama by Grenadian playwright Eljon Wardally, directed by Jackie Alexander with a score by Étienne Charles. Co-produced by Woodie King Jr.'s New Federal Theatre and NC Black Repertory Company.

events.title: Romeo and Juliet — Free Shakespeare in the Park
events.description: Directed by Black Kenyan-American director Saheem Ali, with Tony winner LaChanze and Hamilton's Okieriete Onaodowan. Free outdoor Shakespeare. Final weeks.

events.title: Ailey Extension Afro'Dance — TSQ LIVE
events.description: Free outdoor African and Afro-Caribbean dance class hosted by the Ailey Extension as part of Times Square Alliance's TSQ LIVE series. Open to all.

events.title: Finding Light — National Symphonic Chorus
events.description: Choral concert anchored by works from three celebrated Black American composers — Rosephanye Powell, André Thomas, and Marques L.A. Garrett. Part of Carnegie Hall's United in Sound: America at 250 festival.

events.title: Take 6 — Blue Note Jazz Festival
events.description: Six-time Grammy-winning a cappella group with a catalog spanning gospel, jazz, and R&B. Four nights at the Blue Note.

events.title: Durand Bernarr — Blue Note Jazz Festival
events.description: One of the most singular vocal artists in contemporary Black music, rooted in jazz and R&B. Blue Note Jazz Festival.

events.title: Billie Holiday Theatre Summerfest: Skylight Open
events.description: Annual Summerfest opens with a free night of performance, arts access, and community. One of Brooklyn's foundational Black arts institutions.

events.title: Seneca Village Juneteenth Performance

events.description: Site-specific performance at the exact location of Seneca Village, the Black community seized by the city to build Central Park in 1857. Music, dance, spoken word, and history on the ground where it happened.

events.title: Jamel Gaines Creative Outlet — Juneteenth Performance
events.address: W 249th St & Independence Ave, Riverdale, Bronx

events.title: Studio Museum in Harlem: Juneteenth Community Day
events.description: Full day of free programming including performances, artmaking, and access to all four current exhibitions.

events.title: Oh Sankofa: A Juneteenth Celebration
events.description: Curated by Carl Hancock Rux. Music, choral performance, dance, and storytelling across the history of Black American culture.

events.title: I Dream a Dream That Dreams Back at Me — Juneteenth Celebration
events.description: Original music by Nona Hendryx and Vernon Reid, lyrics by Pulitzer Prize winner Lynn Nottage. Vocalists Nona Hendryx, Marcelle Davies-Lashley, and Kimberly Nichole. Unfolds in four parts across the campus.

events.title: Our Road to Freedom: Jab, J'ouvert, Revelry and Resistance
events.description: CCCADI, one of the city's most important African-diaspora cultural institutions, marks its 50th anniversary year with a program tracing freedom traditions across the Caribbean diaspora.

events.title: Yinka Esi Graves: The Disappearing Act
events.dates: Sat, June 20 · 7:30 PM · Sun, June 21 · 4:00 PM
events.description: Solo performance with live music tracing flamenco's Afro-descendant origins, by British performer of Ghanaian/Jamaican descent. Audio description available June 21.

events.title: Patti LaBelle, Lady Wray, MORERNBPLEASE
events.venue: BRIC Celebrate Brooklyn!, Lena Horne Bandshell
events.description: Patti LaBelle headlines this benefit concert at the Lena Horne Bandshell, with Lady Wray and MORERNBPLEASE. A major night of Black vocal heritage in one of Brooklyn's most beloved outdoor venues.

events.title: Nightbirds: The Music of Labelle
events.venue: Wu Tsai Theater, David Geffen Hall, Lincoln Center
events.description: Original Labelle founding member Nona Hendryx performs songs from a developing rock opera, joined by Ledisi and Olivier Award winner Adrienne Warren.

events.title: Between the Lines: A Conversation with Mara Brock Akil
events.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
events.description: A rare conversation with Mara Brock Akil — creator of Girlfriends, Being Mary Jane, and The Game — one of the most significant Black women storytellers in American television.

events.description: Tony Award-winning revival. Joshua Henry won Best Actor for his role as Coalhouse Walker Jr. Ragtime also won Best Revival of a Musical.

events.title: Cats: The Jellicle Ball — Broadway
events.description: Reimagined through Black and Latinx ballroom and voguing culture. Qween Jean's costume design made her the first openly transgender Tony winner. Nine total nominations.

events.title: Every Brilliant Thing — Tracee Ellis Ross Broadway Debut
events.description: Tracee Ellis Ross's Broadway debut in this intimate solo show. Limited 40-performance run.

events.title: Othello — Classical Theatre of Harlem

events.dates: Previews July 2–3 · Runs July 5–26, Tue–Sun 8:30 PM

events.title: SHABAKA / Kokoroko / Omar / Lovie
events.description: Four major Black British artists across jazz, Afrobeat, and soul. In association with Giant Step and Blue Note Jazz Festival.

events.description: A concert marking what would have been Louis Armstrong's 125th birthday, presented as part of America at 250 programming.

events.title: International African Arts Festival — 55th Annual

events.description: One of Brooklyn's longest-running celebrations of African and African diasporic arts and culture. Theme: HANGANENI (Unity). Live music, dance, spoken word, fashion, and marketplace.

events.title: Daniel J. Watts: Process of Saying Yes
events.description: A visual and process-based exhibition by Tony-nominated actor, tap dancer, and playwright Daniel J. Watts, known for Tina: The Tina Turner Musical and Hamilton.

news.title: Obama Presidential Center Opens on Juneteenth with Major Black Artist Commissions
news.summary: The Obama Presidential Center opens June 19 in Chicago's Jackson Park. The 19.3-acre, $850 million campus is anchored by commissions from Theaster Gates — a frieze drawing from the Ebony and Jet archives — Njideka Akunyili Crosby's official Obama portraits, Rashid Johnson, Lorna Simpson, and Martin Puryear. The opening ceremony June 18 featured The Roots and Stevie Wonder.

news.title: Ruben Santiago-Hudson Wins Tony for Best Featured Actor in a Play
news.summary: Ruben Santiago-Hudson won Best Featured Actor in a Play for Joe Turner's Come and Gone, the August Wilson revival directed by Debbie Allen. The production received five total nominations, including Debbie Allen for Best Direction and Paul Tazewell for Costume Design.

news.title: Joshua Henry Wins Tony for Best Actor in a Musical
news.summary: Joshua Henry won Best Actor in a Musical for Ragtime, the revival centered on Black American life at the turn of the 20th century. Ragtime also won Best Revival of a Musical.

news.title: Qween Jean Becomes First Openly Trans Person to Win a Tony Award
news.summary: Qween Jean, the Black trans costume designer behind Cats: The Jellicle Ball, won Best Costume Design of a Musical at the 79th Tony Awards — the first openly transgender person to win a Tony in the ceremony's 79-year history. Qween Jean is also founder of Black Trans Liberation. Cats: The Jellicle Ball received nine total nominations.

news.title: Dallas Black Dance Theatre Names New Executive Director
news.summary: Kristie Patton Foster appointed executive director of Dallas Black Dance Theatre, following Zenetta Drew's retirement after nearly 40 years. Follows a 2024 union dispute, mass firing, and $560,000 NLRB settlement.

news.title: Kennedy Center Workers Remove Trump Name Following Court Order
news.summary: A federal judge ruled in late May that Trump's name must be removed from the Kennedy Center, citing that only Congress can change the name. Workers began physical removal in mid-June after the deadline passed.

news.title: NEA Anti-DEI Restrictions Force Arts Groups to Choose Between Funding and Values
news.summary: Under Executive Order 14398, arts organizations receiving federal funds must certify they don't operate DEI programs. The NEA cut the Challenge America program, which historically served underserved communities. Over 460 artists signed a protest letter; Black-serving arts institutions are in a particularly untenable position.

news.title: With NEA Funding Slashed, Arts Institutions Serving Black Communities Face an Uncertain Future
news.summary: ARTnews documents how NEA funding cuts are falling hardest on Black arts institutions. Most operate without cash reserves or endowments, making them uniquely exposed when federal grants are cut.

news.title: NYC Arts Groups Face 'Existential' Challenge with Trump Cuts
news.summary: NYC arts organizations report $5 million in lost funding from terminated NEA grants, including Classical Theater of Harlem. For small organizations, a single $35,000 grant can represent 17% of annual budget. Private foundations have begun providing bridge grants.

news.title: Rene Matić Wins Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation Prize 2026
news.summary: Black British photographer Rene Matić won the £30,000 Deutsche Börse Photography Foundation Prize for the exhibition 'AS OPPOSED TO THE TRUTH' at CCA Berlin — the first British winner in over a decade. Work examines race, gender, intimacy, and subcultures.
meta: First UK Winner in a Decade

news.title: Dreamgirls Broadway Revival in Development with Camille A. Brown
news.summary: A Dreamgirls revival is planned for fall 2026, directed and choreographed by five-time Tony nominee Camille A. Brown. A worldwide casting search for Deena, Lorell, and Effie has been underway since fall 2025.

news.title: Magnitude & Bond Study Documents Crisis in Black Literary Arts Funding
news.summary: Cave Canem partnered with Ithaka S+R to publish a field study of Black literary arts organizations, documenting structural funding gaps and what is needed to sustain them, supported by the Wallace Foundation.

news.title: BCALA Literary Awards Announced at ALA Conference
news.summary: The Black Caucus of the American Library Association announced its 2026 Literary Awards. Shonda Buchanan won Best Poetry for 'The Lost Songs of Nina Simone.' Addie E. Citchens won the 1st Novelist Award for 'Dominion: A Novel.'

appointments.name: Kristie Patton Foster
appointments.role: Executive Director, Dallas Black Dance Theatre
appointments.description: First executive director at DBDT following a significant labor dispute, succeeding Zenetta Drew after nearly 40 years. Company approaches its 50th season.

appointments.name: Lisa Brown Ross
appointments.role: President & CEO, African American Museum of Dallas
appointments.description: Effective July 21, 2026. Leadership at one of the country's dedicated African American museums.

appointments.name: Lynda Roscoe Hartigan
appointments.description: Takes the SAAM director role September 8, 2026. Previously developed SAAM's collection of American folk art and African American art.

appointments.name: Alicia Graf Mack
appointments.role: Artistic Director, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater
appointments.description: Only the fourth person to hold this role in 67 years. The position is now endowed at $10 million.

appointments.name: Camille A. Brown
appointments.description: Five-time Tony nominee (Hell's Kitchen, for colored girls, Gypsy) leading the planned fall 2026 Dreamgirls revival.

appointments.name: Koyo Kouoh
appointments.description: First African woman selected to curate the Venice Biennale. Her vision — 'In Minor Keys' — being realized by her team through November 2026.

exhibitions.title: Fade — Seventeen Early-Career Artists of African and Afro-Latinx Descent
exhibitions.description: The sixth installment of the Studio Museum's acclaimed 'F' series. Where the next generation of Black visual art is being seen.

exhibitions.title: Kapwani Kiwanga: BLEED
exhibitions.description: Site-specific commission inspired by quilting traditions and the 'flying geese' pattern, a symbol of the Underground Railroad.

exhibitions.title: From Now: A Collection in Context
exhibitions.description: Over 800 works from the Studio Museum's permanent collection, putting Black artistic production across generations in direct conversation.

exhibitions.title: Ideas of Africa: Portraiture and Political Imagination
exhibitions.description: Seydou Keïta, Malick Sidibé, Kwame Brathwaite, Njideka Akunyili Crosby, and others. One of the most significant photography exhibitions currently in New York. Closes July 25.

exhibitions.title: Pitch Black: Haiti + Congo Revisited
exhibitions.description: Brooklyn's only contemporary art museum dedicated to African diasporic art. Newly opened exhibition on Haitian and Congolese artistic and cultural history.

exhibitions.title: Whitney Biennial 2026
exhibitions.description: The flagship survey of American contemporary art, curated by Marcela Guerrero and Drew Sawyer. Several Black artists represented.

exhibitions.title: Works on Paper — Group Exhibition
exhibitions.description: Group exhibition at one of New York's most dedicated Black-owned contemporary galleries. Nearly two decades centering Black voices. Closes July 11.

exhibitions.title: Louise Mandumbwa: A world in the creases of my palms
exhibitions.description: Intimate photographic and installation work by Black Botswanan-Zambian artist Louise Mandumbwa. Closes July 19.

exhibitions.title: The Seventh AIM Biennial: Forms of Connection
exhibitions.description: Emerging Bronx-based artists, including artists of African descent, from one of the most respected fellowship programs for emerging Bronx artists. Free year-round.
